_meta.note: Captured off the wire: `mimo acp` 0.1.15 (npm @mimo-ai/cli, linux-arm64) driven over stdio by a probe client, `MIMOCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` carrying `permission: ask`. The model was served through a loopback LiteLLM proxy (1.105.1) in front of Amazon Bedrock Claude Haiku 4.5, named to the harness as an openai-compatible provider `probe/probe-model`, so `cost` reads 0. Kiro Crew's own code built the session/new array, in an isolated home. The session is a crewmate WORKER. Its array is mimocode_projection('kirocrew-mate-worker', session_key=<the worker's key>), which read mate_worker.worker_session_spec: a worker base (prompt 'You are the worker.', tools [fs_read], no servers) merged with a crewmate file `pixel` (tools [@pixel-probe], one stdio MCP server whose one tool returns kumquat-17, and a prompt telling the worker to call that tool when asked for the release codeword). The array carried exactly one element, `pixel-probe`; the same projection with no session key carried none. The prompt text was the [AGENT SYSTEM PROMPT] block context_assembly.agent_spec._crewmate_worker_prompt built for that worker with the prompt-in-context channel recorded: the base, the worker principles, then the crewmate's sentence, followed by 'What is the release codeword?'. The model called `pixel-probe_pixel-probe_codeword` after one permission request, and the completed tool_call_update's rawOutput is kumquat-17. Reductions: session, message and tool-call ids replaced with fixed synthetic values; the probe's working directory written as ~/mimo-proj; the `model` select cut to its current value; available_commands_update dropped; consecutive agent_message_chunk frames of one message folded into one frame. `agentInfo.name` is the harness's own answer: the fork still reports `OpenCode`.
